sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·荣森，欢迎收听《重构者》，一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 早在黑胶唱片时代的夜总会里当DJ时，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每晚都要带着300件你最珍爱的藏品去上班，把DJ台变成一个美丽的、拥有50年历史的古董移动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你喜爱的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Rachel Abrams and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是蕾切尔·艾布拉姆斯，这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: The latest release of files related to the sex offender Jeffrey Epstein left key questions about his rise to power and his connections to the president unanswered.
sentences.zh: 最新解密的与性犯罪者杰弗里·爱泼斯坦相关的文件，对他的发迹史以及他与总统的联系留下了关键的未解之谜。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague David Enrich explains how he and a team of reporters worked to fill in those mysteries and reveal the truth about Jeffrey Epstein's origins.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事大卫·恩里奇将解释他和记者团队如何努力填补这些谜团，并揭开杰弗里·爱泼斯坦身世的真相。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, December 23rd.
sentences.zh: 今天是12月23日，星期二。

sentences.en: David Enrich, welcome to the show.
sentences.zh: 大卫·恩里奇，欢迎来到节目。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: David, I think this is probably your fourth or fifth appearance on the show this year to talk about Jeffrey Epstein.
sentences.zh: 大卫，我想这大概是你今年第四次或第五次上我们的节目来谈论杰弗里·爱泼斯坦了。

sentences.en: And this time we're having you back because on Friday, there was obviously this massive file release from the Justice Department that,
sentences.zh: 而这次我们请你回来，是因为在周五，司法部显然发布了这批庞大的文件，

sentences.en: as far as I understand it, did not really advance our understanding of Jeffrey Epstein or his crimes or the people in his orbit.
sentences.zh: 据我理解，这些文件并没有真正增进我们对杰弗里·爱泼斯坦、他的罪行或他身边人的了解。

sentences.en: Can you tell us what you think the biggest takeaways were?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我们，你认为其中最大的收获是什么吗？

sentences.en: It's a hard question because there were not huge takeaways.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很难的问题，因为并没有什么巨大的收获。

sentences.en: And we got lots of bits of incremental color and detail that reinforced the deep depravity of Epstein's crimes and the horrible things he was doing.
sentences.zh: 我们得到了许多零星的增量色彩和细节，这些都强化了爱泼斯坦罪行的极度堕落以及他所做的可怕事情。

sentences.en: We also got some new tidbits.
sentences.zh: 我们也看到了一些新的小道消息。

sentences.en: We saw, for example, Bill Clinton in numerous photos with Epstein and his associates, including in a swimming pool.
sentences.zh: 例如，我们看到比尔·克林顿与爱泼斯坦及其同伙在许多照片中出现，其中包括在一个游泳池里。

sentences.en: We saw that one of Epstein's victims back in 1996 had reported him to the FBI for having child sexual abuse material.
sentences.zh: 我们看到爱泼斯坦的一位受害者早在1996年就曾向联邦调查局举报他拥有儿童性虐待材料。

sentences.en: And that's a decade before we know the federal prosecutors actually started investigating Epstein.
sentences.zh: 而这在我们所知的联邦检察官实际开始调查爱泼斯坦之前的一个十年。

sentences.en: So that was definitely a new development.
sentences.zh: 所以这绝对是一个新的进展。

sentences.en: But for the most part, there was nothing here that fundamentally altered our understanding of Epstein and his network.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，这里没有什么东西从根本上改变了我们对爱泼斯坦及其网络的理解。

sentences.en: And notably, also, very little about Donald Trump, whose name was barely mentioned in these files.
sentences.zh: 值得注意的是，关于唐纳德·特朗普的信息也非常少，这些文件中几乎没有提到他的名字。

sentences.en: And it was Trump's relationship with Epstein that triggered a lot of the political interest in this investigation to begin with.
sentences.zh: 正是特朗普与爱泼斯坦的关系，一开始引发了人们对这项调查的巨大政治兴趣。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Just to remind people, this whole file release is coming about because of a massive pressure campaign, mostly from Democrats, but also from some within the MAGA orbit,
sentences.zh: 提醒大家一下，这次文件的整体公开是因为一场大规模的施压运动，主要来自民主党人，但也有一部分来自MAGA阵营内部的人，

sentences.en: for Donald Trump and his administration to release the so-called Epstein files.
sentences.zh: 要求唐纳德·特朗普及其政府公开所谓的爱泼斯坦文件。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that basically forced Trump to sign legislation authorizing these files to be released from the Justice Department.
sentences.zh: 这基本上迫使特朗普签署了立法，授权司法部公开这些文件。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's worth noting that the Justice Department did not do what it was legally required to do, which was release all of the files.
sentences.zh: 是的，值得注意的是，司法部没有做法律要求它做的事情，也就是公开所有文件。

sentences.en: And those files that were released were, in many cases, so heavily redacted that you couldn't make any sense of them.
sentences.zh: 而那些被公开的文件在许多情况下被严重涂黑，以至于你根本无法理解它们的意思。

sentences.en: And why didn't they release them?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么不公开？

sentences.en: The Justice Department has said that they will release the rest of the files on kind of a rolling basis over the next few weeks and that they need this additional time to be able to properly review and redact these huge quantities of materials.
sentences.zh: 司法部曾表示，他们将在接下来的几周内以某种滚动发布的方式公布其余文件，并且他们需要额外的时间来适当地审查和涂黑这些大量的材料。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So, knowing that there would be this sort of staggered release, what were you expecting to get?
sentences.zh: 那么，既然知道会是这种分批发布的形式，你当时期待得到什么？

sentences.en: Or maybe more importantly, what questions were you hoping that this batch of files would actually answer?
sentences.zh: 或者更重要的是，你希望这批文件能真正解答哪些问题？

sentences.en: I mean, it depends on your perspective and what your interest is in this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这取决于你的视角以及你对此的兴趣所在。

sentences.en: I mean, I think one of the biggest questions that many victims have and many people who have been focusing on Epstein for a while are,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为许多受害者和许多关注爱泼斯坦一段时间的人最大的疑问之一是，

sentences.en: are there other men who were enabling him or participating in sex crimes with him?
sentences.zh: 是否还有其他男人在怂恿他或与他一起参与性犯罪？

sentences.en: And for me and my colleagues, I've been working with Matt Goldstein, Jessica Silver-Greenberg,
sentences.zh: 对于我和我的同事们来说——我已经和马特·戈德斯坦、杰西卡·西尔弗-格林伯格

sentences.en: and Steve Eater for months now to really understand Epstein's financial web that he wove and looking at his origins and how he went from kind of this rags to riches story where he managed to transform himself from a working class family into an extraordinarily rich and well-connected person.
sentences.zh: 以及史蒂夫·伊特合作数月，旨在真正了解爱泼斯坦编织的金融网络，并研究他的出身，以及他是如何从一个经历过“白手起家”故事的人，成功把自己从一个工人阶级家庭转变成一个极其富有且人脉极广的人的。

sentences.en: And so, we were wondering if there would be any revelations in these files about that, and we're just completely disappointed in that regard.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们想知道这些文件中是否会有关于这方面的任何揭秘，而在这方面我们完全感到失望。

sentences.en: Well, the reporting that you mentioned is what I want to talk to you about because everybody's been eagerly awaiting the release of these files, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你提到的报道正是我想要跟你谈的，因为每个人都在热切期待这些文件的发布，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, hoping perhaps that the files would address some of these enduring questions about Epstein and his crimes.
sentences.zh: 就像是希望这些文件能够解决关于爱泼斯坦及其罪行的某些挥之不去的问题。

sentences.en: And obviously, that did not happen on Friday.
sentences.zh: 很显然，周五并没有发生这种情况。

sentences.en: But you and our colleagues have been digging into a different period of Epstein's life, one that preceded the era of his most flagrant criminal activity that he became known for,
sentences.zh: 但你和我们的同事一直在深入挖掘爱泼斯坦生命中的另一个时期，一个在他因之闻名、因之被捕的最猖獗犯罪活动时期之前的时期，

sentences.en: that he was arrested for.
sentences.zh: 他正是因为那些活动而被捕的。

sentences.en: Why was that period your focus?
sentences.zh: 为什么那个时期是你们关注的焦点？

sentences.en: Why was it important, in your estimation, to understand the early period of Epstein's life?
sentences.zh: 在你看来，为什么理解爱泼斯坦早期的生活如此重要？

sentences.en: Well, Epstein built an extensive sex trafficking operation all over the world, and that was really expensive, and it required the support of a lot of powerful people.
sentences.zh: 嗯，爱泼斯坦在全世界建立了一个庞大的性走客网络，这是非常昂贵的，并且需要许多有权势的人的支持。

sentences.en: And so, the question for us has been, how did he get in a position where he had the money and the power and the connections to do that?
sentences.zh: 因此，对我们来说，问题一直是：他是如何走到那个拥有资金、权力和人脉来做到这一点的地步的？

sentences.en: But this was a guy who came from a really working-class background.
sentences.zh: 但这家伙出身于一个真正的工人阶级背景。

sentences.en: He grew up in Coney Island in Brooklyn.
sentences.zh: 他在布鲁克林的康尼岛长大。

sentences.en: His dad was an employee of the New York City Parks Department.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲是纽约市公园管理局的一名雇员。

sentences.en: He was really kind of scraping by growing up.
sentences.zh: 他在成长过程中其实可以说是勉强糊口。

sentences.en: And then somehow starts to climb this ladder, which will bring him to the upper echelons of Wall Street and American politics.
sentences.zh: 然后他不知怎么地开始往上爬，这最终将他带到了华尔街和美国政治的上层阶级。

sentences.en: And I think the absence of information about Epstein and his early years has given rise to just a vast number of conspiracy theories,
sentences.zh: 我认为，关于爱泼斯坦及其早年生活的信息的缺乏，引发了大量的阴谋论，

sentences.en: ranging from that Epstein was running the super-sophisticated blackmail operation to that he was affiliated with intelligence services.
sentences.zh: 从爱泼斯坦在运营超级复杂的敲诈勒索行动，到他与情报机构有关联不等。

sentences.en: And the period from basically the mid-1970s to the early 1990s, for the most part, has been just a complete black box.
sentences.zh: 基本上从20世纪70年代中期到90年代初的这段时间，在很大程度上完全是一个黑匣子。

sentences.en: And so, our goal, when we started reporting on this months ago, was to try and get inside that black box and figure out how Epstein got his start.
sentences.zh: 因此，几个月前当我们开始报道此事时，我们的目标就是试图进入那个黑匣子，弄清楚爱泼斯坦是如何起家的。

sentences.en: And the bottom line of how he did that was that he was an extremely successful con man.
sentences.zh: 他之所以能做到这一点的根本原因在于，他是一个极其成功的骗子。

sentences.en: He stole, he deceived, he manipulated, and he learned over and over again that he could do so basically with impunity.
sentences.zh: 他偷窃、欺骗、操纵，并且一次又一次地了解到，他基本上可以毫无后果地这样做。

sentences.en: So, where does the story begin?
sentences.zh: 那么，这个故事是从哪里开始的呢？

sentences.en: It begins in 1976.
sentences.zh: 它始于1976年。

sentences.en: Epstein is a teacher at the Dalton School in Manhattan, and he gets invited to a reception at an art gallery.
sentences.zh: 爱泼斯坦是曼哈顿道尔顿学校的一名老师，他受邀参加一个艺术画廊的招待会。

sentences.en: And he goes kind of grudgingly in his tongue.
sentences.zh: 他有点勉强地去了，心里带着讽刺。

sentences.en: And at the reception, he bumps into the parent of one of his students who is impressed with his math chops.
sentences.zh: 在招待会上，他撞见了自己一个学生的家长，这位家长对他的数学才能印象深刻。

sentences.en: And the parent suggests that maybe he is wasting his time being a teacher and instead should consider a career in Wall Street.
sentences.zh: 这位家长暗示，他当老师或许是在浪费时间，反而应该考虑去华尔街发展。

sentences.en: And the parent then introduces Epstein to a guy named Ace Greenberg.
sentences.zh: 随后，这位家长把爱泼斯坦介绍给了一个叫埃斯·格林伯格的人。

sentences.en: Very big name.
sentences.zh: 一个非常大的人物。

sentences.en: Yeah, who at the time was a top executive at Bear Stearns, which is this scrappy Wall Street investment bank.
sentences.zh: 是的，他当时是贝尔斯登公司的顶级高管，这是一家敢打敢拼的华尔街投资银行。

sentences.en: And one of the ways in which it's scrappy is that it is not going to hire Ivy League MBAs.
sentences.zh: 它敢打敢拼的方式之一就是它不雇佣常春藤盟校的MBA。

sentences.en: It is looking for what Ace Greenberg likes to call PSDs, which stands for poor, smart, and deeply desirous of being rich.
sentences.zh: 它寻找的是埃斯·格林伯格喜欢称之为PSD的人，代表着出身贫寒、聪明伶俐、极度渴望变富。

sentences.en: And Epstein goes in to meet Greenberg for a job interview.
sentences.zh: 爱泼斯坦去见格林伯格进行工作面试。

sentences.en: And Epstein fits the bill.
sentences.zh: 而爱泼斯坦完全符合条件。

sentences.en: Greenberg is bowled over by the guy's charisma and charm and apparent math prowess and offers him a job.
sentences.zh: 格林伯格被这家伙的个人魅力、吸引力以及明显的数学才能彻底倾倒，并给了他一份工作。

sentences.en: So he arrives at Bear Stearns and he quickly becomes the protege to some of the firm's top executives.
sentences.zh: 于是他来到贝尔斯登，并迅速成为该行一些顶级高管的门生。

sentences.en: One is Greenberg, the guy who hired him, who is so taken with Epstein that he introduces him to his own 20-year-old daughter.
sentences.zh: 一个是格林伯格，也就是雇佣他的人，他非常喜欢爱泼斯坦，以至于把他介绍给了自己20岁的女儿。

sentences.en: And they start dating, which affords Epstein something akin to protected status at the firm.
sentences.zh: 他们开始约会，这为爱泼斯坦在公司争取到了一种类似于受保护的地位。

sentences.en: And that really quickly comes in handy because within a couple of months of his arrival at Bear Stearns, Epstein's boss, a guy named Michael Tenenbaum,
sentences.zh: 这很快就派上了用场，因为在来到贝尔斯登几个月内，爱泼斯坦的老板，一个叫迈克尔·特嫩鲍姆的人，

sentences.en: learns from the HR department that Epstein had lied on his resume about having graduated from college.
sentences.zh: 从人力资源部门得知，爱泼斯坦在简历上谎称自己大学毕业。

sentences.en: And so Tenenbaum summons Epstein into his office, is not really sure what to do about this because, you know, this is a very serious infraction.
sentences.zh: 于是特嫩鲍姆把爱泼斯坦叫进办公室，其实不太确定该怎么处理这件事，因为，你知道，这是一个非常严重的违规行为。

sentences.en: On the other hand, the guy is dating the boss's daughter and confronts Epstein with this, expecting Epstein to lie and dissemble and deny,
sentences.zh: 另一方面，这家伙正在和老板的女儿约会，他拿着这件事质问爱泼斯坦，期待爱泼斯坦撒谎、伪装和否认，

sentences.en: which in that case would allow Tenenbaum to easily fire him.
sentences.zh: 那样的话，特嫩鲍姆就可以轻松地解雇他了。

sentences.en: Instead, Epstein says, you're right.
sentences.zh: 相反，爱泼斯坦说，你是对的。

sentences.en: It's true.
sentences.zh: 这是真的。

sentences.en: I did lie.
sentences.zh: 我确实撒谎了。

sentences.en: And the reason he lied, Epstein goes on to say, is that if he didn't lie,
sentences.zh: 爱泼斯坦接着说，他撒谎的原因是，如果他不撒谎，

sentences.en: there is no way a firm like Bear Stearns or anyone else is going to give him a chance without having a college diploma.
sentences.zh: 像贝尔斯登这样的公司或任何其他人，根本不可能在没有大学文凭的情况下给他一个机会。

sentences.en: And Tenenbaum is so taken aback and disarmed by this honesty that he decides to give Epstein a second chance.
sentences.zh: 特嫩鲍姆被这种诚实弄得大为惊讶和卸下防备，以至于他决定给爱泼斯坦第二次机会。

sentences.en: And this is a pattern we will see repeating over and over and over again.
sentences.zh: 这是一个我们将看到一遍又一遍重复的模式。

sentences.en: It's sort of remarkable because, first of all, he gets this job because, in a way, Ace Greenberg is like fetishizing his lower middle class background, right?
sentences.zh: 这有点引人注目，首先，他得到这份工作是因为，在某种程度上，埃斯·格林伯格就像是在迷恋他的中下阶层背景，对吧？

sentences.en: Something that would have been a disadvantage to somebody else is an advantage to Epstein.
sentences.zh: 对别人来说可能是劣势的东西，对爱泼斯坦来说却是优势。

sentences.en: He gets his foot in the door.
sentences.zh: 他成功踏入了门槛。

sentences.en: And then when he gets caught, he doesn't just make himself sympathetic.
sentences.zh: 然后当他被抓包时，他不仅让自己变得值得同情。

sentences.en: He actually makes himself a victim of the institution where he's working, right?
sentences.zh: 他实际上把自己变成了他所工作的那家机构的受害者，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, I had no choice but to lie.
sentences.zh: 就像是，我别无选择，只能撒谎。

sentences.en: Otherwise, you, big, powerful, mean Wall Street bank, would never have taken a chance on me.
sentences.zh: 否则，你们这些庞大、有权势、刻薄的华尔街银行，绝不会给我一个机会。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And to Tenenbaum, you know, this is now, what, 40 or 45 years later, when I spoke to him, he was still kind of marveling at Epstein's knack for understanding human dynamics.
sentences.zh: 对特嫩鲍姆来说，你知道，现在，大概是40或45年之后，当我与他交谈时，他仍然对爱泼斯坦理解人类动态的诀窍感到惊叹。

sentences.en: So, well, just on the spur of the moment, he understood that that would be something that was likely to get him a second chance.
sentences.zh: 所以，就在那一瞬间，他明白这很可能是为他赢得第二次机会的事情。

sentences.en: And sure enough, it worked.
sentences.zh: 果不其然，成功了。

sentences.en: So what happens next?
sentences.zh: 那么接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, he keeps his job and he starts very quickly climbing through the ranks at Bear Stearns.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他保住了工作，并开始在贝尔斯登迅速晋升。

sentences.en: Within a few years, he has been named a limited partner, which means that he is getting paid boatloads of money at that point.
sentences.zh: 几年之内，他被任命为有限合伙人，这意味着他在那个时候赚取了大量的金钱。

sentences.en: Something like $800,000 in today's dollars.
sentences.zh: 相当于当今价值约80万美元。

sentences.en: And yet the problems still keep bubbling up.
sentences.zh: 然而问题仍然不断浮出水面。

sentences.en: And Epstein was found to abuse his expense account.
sentences.zh: 人们发现爱泼斯坦滥用他的费用账户。

sentences.en: He took a work trip to the Caribbean and charged Bear Stearns something like $10,000 on jewelry and clothing for his girlfriend.
sentences.zh: 他去加勒比海进行了一次工作旅行，在贝尔斯登报销了大约1万美元用于给他女友买珠宝和服装。

sentences.en: So this is after he was dating the boss's daughter.
sentences.zh: 所以这是在他跟老板女儿约会之后的事。

sentences.en: Another thing is that it turns out that he has been helping his girlfriend get early access to lucrative investment deals at Bear Stearns,
sentences.zh: 另一件事是，事实证明他一直在帮他的女友提前获得贝尔斯登公司有利可图的投资交易，

sentences.en: which is a violation certainly of the company's rules, if not the law.

sentences.zh: 为了避免这种羞辱，他决定辞职，并表示他甚至遭到调查这一事实让他感到深深的冒犯。

sentences.en: So one of the many things he learned at Bear Stearns through this network of acquaintances and colleagues that he built up was basically how to act and behave as a really rich person.

sentences.zh: 但这也是为了拥有那种自信，即他属于这些环境，属于这些与富有和有权势的人共处的房间。

sentences.zh: 一位前贝尔斯登同事把他介绍给了一个叫迈克尔·斯特罗尔的人，后者是一名视频游戏高管。

sentences.zh: 爱泼斯坦说服斯特罗尔交给他45万美元，大约占斯特罗尔净资产的10%，用来投资爱泼斯坦声称的一笔石油交易。

sentences.zh: 而斯特罗尔几乎输光了所有的钱，并不断纠缠爱泼斯坦，说，我的钱在哪里？

sentences.zh: 你答应过我们能得到这种回报的。

sentences.en: Epstein rebuffs him over and over again.
sentences.zh: 爱泼斯坦一次又一次地拒绝他。

sentences.zh: 在某个时候，甚至给他寄了一品脱原油，以说服他石油交易确实存在。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: But the money is just gone, ultimately.
sentences.zh: 但最终钱就是没了。

sentences.en: And so this is one of Epstein's huge first killings.
sentences.zh: 所以这是爱泼斯坦赚到的第一笔巨款之一。

sentences.en: He walks away with what appears to be several hundred thousand dollars of money that he just stole from this guy.
sentences.zh: 他带着据信有几十万美元的资金扬长而去，这些钱是他从这家伙身上偷来的。

sentences.en: And nothing really happens.
sentences.zh: 而实际上什么也没有发生。

sentences.en: And Stroll files a lawsuit against him.
sentences.zh: 斯特罗尔对提起诉讼。

sentences.zh: 这在联邦法院系统里来回踢皮球多年。

sentences.en: Ultimately, Epstein prevails on technical grounds.
sentences.zh: 最终，爱泼斯坦在技术层面上胜诉了。

sentences.en: And so Epstein is now two for two.
sentences.zh: 所以爱泼斯坦现在是二战二胜。

sentences.en: He cheated and lied at Bear Stearns and essentially got away with it.
sentences.zh: 他在贝尔斯登作弊和撒谎，基本上逃脱了惩罚。

sentences.zh: 现在他在这个视频游戏高管身上作弊和撒谎，再次带着他的钱逍遥法外。

sentences.en: And for someone like Epstein, the message there is very clear, which is that if you lie and cheat well enough and often enough and are sufficiently manipulative,
sentences.zh: 对于像爱泼斯坦这样的人来说，其中的信息非常明确，那就是如果你谎言说得足够好、足够频繁且极具操纵性，

sentences.zh: 你完全可以靠这个过上很好的生活。

sentences.en: So he's not only learning that he can get away with it,
sentences.zh: 所以他不仅了解到他可以逃脱惩罚，

sentences.en: but it sounds like he's learning that he's getting away with it at a larger level and with people who are arguably within his social network.
sentences.zh: 听起来他还了解到他正在以更高的水平逃脱惩罚，而且对象可以说是他社交网络内的人。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.zh: 爱泼斯坦可谓是诈骗和偷盗方面的一个极佳的学习者。

sentences.en: And you can see him progressing from one stage of this to the next and getting more ambitious and bolder and bolder the more times he pulls this off and the more times he gets away with it.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到他从这一阶段晋升到下一阶段，随着他一次次得手，一次次逃脱惩罚，他变得越来越有野心，也越来越大胆。

sentences.en: So where does he go from here?
sentences.zh: 那么他接下来要去哪里？

sentences.en: So Epstein around this time has been referring to himself as a financial bounty hunter, basically someone who like tracks down hidden assets all over the world.
sentences.zh: 所以当时的爱泼斯坦把自己称为金融赏金猎人，基本上就像是一个在世界各地追查隐藏资产的人。

sentences.en: And as it happens, we're in the early 1980s at this point.
sentences.zh: 碰巧的是，此时正值20世纪80年代初。

sentences.en: He is dating a Spanish actress named Anna Obregon.
sentences.zh: 他在和一个名叫安娜·奥布雷贡的西班牙女演员交往。

sentences.zh: 结果她的家人刚刚发现，由于纽约一家证券公司倒闭，他们损失了数百万美元。

sentences.en: And so they hire Epstein to track down their missing money.
sentences.zh: 于是他们雇佣爱泼斯坦去追查他们失踪的资金。

sentences.zh: 他与他的一个朋友搭档，那人曾是一名联邦检察官。

sentences.en: And together they spend the next couple of years trying to track down these missing assets.
sentences.zh: 两人在接下来的几年里一起试图追回这些失踪的资产。

sentences.en: And lo and behold, they find them.
sentences.zh: 结果呢，他们竟然真的找到了。

sentences.en: They're in a bank in the Cayman Islands.
sentences.zh: 它们在开曼群岛的一家银行里。

sentences.en: And Epstein and his buddy charter a jet, go down to Cayman, and somehow walk away with millions of dollars of these securities.
sentences.zh: 爱泼斯坦和他的死党包了一架喷气式飞机，飞到开曼群岛，不知怎么地就拿走了这几百万美元的证券。

sentences.en: They recover it and get paid a certain portion of that as a fee.
sentences.zh: 他们追回了资金，并作为报酬获得了其中的一部分。

sentences.en: And so Epstein by this point is almost certainly a millionaire,
sentences.zh: 因此到这个时候，爱泼斯坦几乎可以确定已经是个百万富翁了，

sentences.en: which is really – it's quite an extraordinary turnaround for a guy who just a few years earlier was this working-class guy trying to make a living as a high school teacher.
sentences.zh: 这真的是——对一个几年前还是个试图靠当高中老师谋生的普通工人阶级男子来说，这是一个相当惊人的转变。

sentences.en: The story of the recovered money, though, is also so interesting because one of the narratives about Epstein in recent years, in recent memory,
sentences.zh: 不过，追回资金的故事也非常有趣，因为近年来、在人们的记忆中，关于爱泼斯坦的种种说法之一，

sentences.en: is that this guy was not actually a financial genius.
sentences.zh: 就是这家伙其实并不是什么金融天才。

sentences.en: That's the thing you hear over and over again.
sentences.zh: 这是你一遍又一遍听到的话。

sentences.en: People are like, why would these billionaires hand him millions of dollars to manage when he wasn't proving himself as singular in any particular way?
sentences.zh: 人们都在想，既然他在任何特定方面都没有证明过自己的独一无二，为什么这些亿万富翁还要把数百万美元交给他管理？

sentences.en: But this is the only story I think I am familiar with where he really provides tangible value to people in a way that does seem quite singular.
sentences.zh: 但据我所知，这是唯一一个让我熟悉的、他真正以一种似乎相当独特的方式为人们提供切实价值的故事。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And to be frank, it's one of the things I've struggled with a little bit in reporting the story and in understanding the story because Epstein,
sentences.zh: 坦白说，这也是我在报道和理解这个故事时感到有些纠结的地方之一，因为爱泼斯坦，

sentences.en: he likes to present himself as this financial genius.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢把自己包装成一个金融天才。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We have not seen evidence to support that claim.
sentences.zh: 我们没有看到支持这一说法的证据。

sentences.en: We do see here some glimmer of cleverness that does set him apart.
sentences.zh: 我们确实在这里看到了他身上闪现的一些聪明才智，这确实让他与众不同。

sentences.en: And so around this time,
sentences.zh: 所以在那个时候左右，

sentences.en: Epstein has amassed enough money that he has gone from having been kind of chased out of Bear Stearns with his tail between his legs to now he returns to Bear Stearns,
sentences.zh: 爱泼斯坦已经积累了足够的财富，他从当年灰溜溜地被赶出贝尔斯登，变成了如今重返贝尔斯登，

sentences.en: this time as a valued client.
sentences.zh: 这一次是以贵宾客户的身份。

sentences.en: He's doing lots of trading through the firm, which produces revenue for Bear Stearns, which makes Bear Stearns very eager to keep him in its good graces.
sentences.zh: 他在该公司进行了大量的交易，这为贝尔斯登带来了收入，使得贝尔斯登非常渴望维持与他的良好关系。

sentences.zh: 嗯，爱泼斯坦在公司的一位前经理现在正负责协助接待他这位客户，手下有一位非常迷人的年轻助理叫帕特里夏·施密特。

sentences.en: And one night in 1987, the manager asks Schmidt to deliver some papers to Epstein's apartment at night.
sentences.zh: 1987年的一天晚上，这位经理让施密特在夜里把一些文件送到爱泼斯坦的公寓。

sentences.en: And Schmidt goes over to the apartment.
sentences.zh: 施密特去了那套公寓。

sentences.zh: 爱泼斯坦给她泡了茶，带她参观了他那栋非常漂亮的公寓楼，并邀请她随时回来使用大楼的游泳池。

sentences.zh: 施密特接受了这个邀请，由此开始了施密特和爱泼斯坦之间长达一年的性关系。

sentences.en: And one of the things we found in our reporting is that the same Bear Stearns manager on multiple other occasions also sent young female assistants over to Epstein's apartment,
sentences.zh: 我们在报道中发现的一件事是，同一位贝尔斯登经理在其他多个场合也曾将年轻的女性助理派往爱泼斯坦的公寓，

sentences.zh: 而这最终都导致了性关系。

sentences.en: And Epstein seems to realize that if Bear Stearns can use women as a source of leverage, so can he.
sentences.zh: 爱泼斯坦似乎意识到，既然贝尔斯登可以把女性作为一种筹码，他也可以。

sentences.en: And Schmidt, when I spoke with her, she was very clear-eyed about her role in this and that she was being used.
sentences.zh: 而施密特和我交谈时，她对自己在其中的角色以及自己被利用这件事看得很透彻。

sentences.en: And the way she described it to me was that I was his plaything, and Epstein perceived her as someone that's going to help him get where he wants to go.
sentences.zh: 她对我的形容是，我是他的玩物，而爱泼斯坦把她看作是能帮他实现目标的人。

sentences.en: And sure enough, we see him start to use Schmidt for other things, such as he would have Schmidt give his clients and acquaintances tours around Wall Street,
sentences.zh: 果不其然，我们看到他开始让施密特做其他事情，比如他会让施密特带他的客户和熟人参观华尔街，

sentences.en: bringing them into Bear Stearns, maybe take them out to a nice dinner.
sentences.zh: 带他们进入贝尔斯登，或者带他们去吃一顿丰盛的晚餐。

sentences.en: And so Epstein had discovered that he could use attractive young women as a potent form of currency as he sought to impress and cultivate relationships with rich and powerful people whom he wanted to do business with.
sentences.zh: 因此，爱泼斯坦发现，当他试图打动和结交那些他想与之做生意的富有且有权势的人时，他可以把迷人的年轻女性作为一种强有力的货币。

sentences.en: He's taking advantage of the fact that other people are motivated by sex, and they might do something for him if he does something for them,
sentences.zh: 他利用了其他人受性欲驱使这一事实，如果他为他们做点什么，他们可能会为他做点什么，

sentences.en: i.e. send this woman out to meetings with them.
sentences.zh: 也就是派这个女人去和他们会面。

sentences.en: As far as we can tell, this is probably the first time that Epstein has really fully discovered his ability to use women to really advance his own agenda.
sentences.zh: 据我们所知，这可能是爱泼斯坦第一次真正充分发现自己有能力利用女性来推进他自己的议程。

sentences.en: And at the same time, around now, Epstein has also really cultivated enough connections and built enough wealth that those things start compounding upon each other.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，大约在这个时候，爱泼斯坦也真正积累了足够的人脉，建立起了足够的财富，以至于这些因素开始相互叠加。

sentences.en: And we will see over the ensuing decade that Epstein really takes that to the next level and starts building connections with kind of the creme de la creme of American finance and society.
sentences.zh: 我们将在随后的十年里看到，爱泼斯坦真正将这一点提升到了一个新的水平，并开始与美国金融和社会的最上层精英建立联系。

sentences.en: And so he'll build and exploit relationships with people like David Rockefeller, like Les Wexner, the retail tycoon, ultimately with big institutions and big banks like J.P.
sentences.zh: 因此，他将与大卫·洛克菲勒、零售大亨莱斯·韦克斯纳等人物建立并利用关系，最终与摩根大通等大型机构和大银行建立关系。

sentences.en: Morgan.

sentences.en: And this is the Epstein who we all now know, right, as someone who has built this huge network, not only of young women and girls whom he's abusing, but also this cast of rich,
sentences.zh: 这就是我们现在都认识的那个爱泼斯坦，对吧，他建立了一个庞大的网络，不仅有他正在虐待的年轻女性和女孩，还有一群富有的、

sentences.zh: 有权势的、有名望的男人们，他们在这一路上支持并纵容了他。

sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 对总统施加的压力正是导致这些文件被公开的原因，

sentences.zh: 因为人们想了解政府掌握了关于杰弗里·爱泼斯坦及其犯罪行为以及他所运作的网络有哪些证据。

sentences.en: And so I wonder, then, how are we to think about where Donald Trump fits into Epstein's early years?
sentences.zh: 那么我想知道，我们该如何看待唐纳德·特朗普在爱泼斯坦早年生活中的角色呢？

sentences.en: Well, Epstein and Trump were operating in very similar social circles for a number of years, basically from the late 1980s into the early 2000s.
sentences.zh: 嗯，爱泼斯坦和特朗普在很多年里都在非常相似的社交圈子里活动，基本上从20世纪80年代末一直持续到21世纪初。

sentences.zh: 他们有时显然是非常亲密的朋友。

sentences.zh: 我们的同事尼克·孔费索里刚刚花了几个月的时间深入挖掘此事。

sentences.zh: 尼克在他的报道中将爱泼斯坦和特朗普描述为彼此的僚机。

sentences.en: That being said, there are still a lot of unanswered questions about the exact nature of that relationship, if there were business dealings between the two of them, for example.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，关于这种关系的具体性质，比如两人之间是否存在商业交易，仍然有很多未解之谜。

sentences.en: And it is not clear to me whether there are answers that are lurking in these as yet undisclosed Epstein files that the Trump administration is sitting on.
sentences.zh: 而且我也不清楚，特朗普政府掌握的这些尚未公开的爱泼斯坦文件中，是否潜藏着答案。

sentences.en: And one way to think about this is that at the outset, what the Justice Department has been told and is required under law to release
sentences.zh: 理解这一点的一个方式是，从一开始，司法部被告知且根据法律要求公开的内容

sentences.en: are files related to the federal investigations of Epstein over the years.
sentences.zh: 是多年来有关联邦对爱泼斯坦调查的文件。

sentences.en: And it is not clear to me that federal investigators were doing a whole lot of investigating into the men
sentences.zh: 我不清楚联邦调查人员是否对那些与爱泼斯坦有关的男性

sentences.en: with whom Epstein was associated, whether that's Trump or men like Leon Black or Les Wexner or people like that.
sentences.zh: 进行了大量的调查，无论是特朗普，还是像利昂·布拉克或莱斯·韦克斯纳这样的人，或者是其他类似的人物。

sentences.en: And so to the extent that those were not subjects of investigation, we're not likely to see a tremendous amount about them in these files.
sentences.zh: 因此，既然这些人不在调查之列，我们不太可能在这些文件中看到关于他们的大量内容。

sentences.en: But at the same time, there's also a question of why exactly Trump and his administration have been so reluctant to come clean about what is in these files to begin with.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，也有一个问题，那就是为什么特朗普及其政府从一开始就如此不愿意坦白这些文件里的内容。

sentences.en: And if they had just released this stuff when they said they would back early in this year, we might not be talking about this anymore.
sentences.zh: 如果他们早听从在今年年初说过的那样直接公开这些东西，我们现在可能就不会再谈论这个了。

sentences.en: And the fact that they have been fighting so hard against full transparency here, it does suggest that there is something in there that they want to hide.
sentences.zh: 他们如此拼命地反对完全透明，这确实表明里面有什么东西是他们想要隐藏的。

sentences.en: But at the same time, one of the things I've never quite understood about the Epstein files, as we have been calling them,
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，关于我们一直所说的爱泼斯坦文件，我有一点一直不太明白，

sentences.en: is if there was evidence of criminal behavior on the part of Trump or any of these other notable figures,
sentences.zh: 那就是如果存在特朗普或任何这些知名人士有犯罪行为的证据，

sentences.en: that has been in the possession of the DOJ across multiple administrations for years.
sentences.zh: 司法部在多届政府期间多年来一直掌握着这些证据。

sentences.en: And so I don't mean to come off as naive and say, like, if the DOJ had evidence of crimes, why would they not investigate it?
sentences.zh: 所以，我不是想显得天真地说，如果司法部有犯罪证据，他们为什么不调查呢？

sentences.en: But I just don't quite understand why exactly we believe that it wouldn't have come out before now.
sentences.zh: 但我只是不太明白，为什么我们确信这些证据在现在之前不会被曝光。

sentences.en: It's not self-evident that this would have already come out for at least two reasons.
sentences.zh: 至少有两个原因表明，这未必一定会早就曝光。

sentences.en: One reason is that, you know, it's become, I think, accepted conventional wisdom that if an administration has damaging information about its political enemies,
sentences.zh: 一个原因是，我想，现在已经成了一种被接受的传统观念，即如果一个政府掌握了关于其政治对手的具有破坏性的信息，

sentences.en: that that will immediately be released.
sentences.zh: 这些信息就会立即被公布。

sentences.en: That is not the way justice departments have historically operated.
sentences.zh: 但司法部历史上并非这样运作的。

sentences.en: And so it's entirely possible that a previous administration's Justice Department might have had damaging information about its opponents that it kept under wraps
sentences.zh: 因此，前政府的司法部完全有可能掌握了有关其对手的负面信息，但将其秘而不宣，

sentences.en: because it was supposed to do so.
sentences.zh: 因为它的职责就是如此。

sentences.en: That's thing one.
sentences.zh: 这是第一点。

sentences.en: Thing two is that it is also entirely possible that there could have been reports or suspicions or investigative trails that were followed that did lead to powerful men
sentences.zh: 第二点是，完全有可能曾经存在过报告、怀疑或顺藤摸瓜的调查线索，并且确实指向了权贵男性

sentences.en: and powerful institutions.
sentences.zh: 和强力机构。

sentences.en: And those investigations went nowhere, maybe because there wasn't evidence, but also it could be because there's a long history of federal investigators
sentences.zh: 而这些调查无果而终，也许是因为没有证据，但也可能是因为联邦调查人员有一个悠久的历史，

sentences.en: not aggressively pursuing cases that involve white-collar defendants.
sentences.zh: 即不对涉及白领被告的案件进行强力追查。

sentences.en: When you have some of the richest, most powerful people in the world, it is not surprising and it's not a conspiracy to think that those people might get away with it.
sentences.zh: 当你拥有世界上一些最富有、最有权势的人时，认为这些人可能会逃脱法律制裁并不令人意外，也不是什么阴谋论。

sentences.en: I guess the reason why I'm sort of lingering on this is that it feels like everybody is waiting for another shoe to drop.
sentences.zh: 我想我之所以纠结于这一点，是因为感觉所有人都在等待另一只靴子落地。

sentences.en: Everyone is waiting with bated breath to see what's in these files and maybe these files will finally answer our persistent questions about Epstein's orbit and Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 每个人都屏息以待，想看看这些文件里究竟有什么，也许这些文件最终能解答我们对爱泼斯坦核心圈子和唐纳德·特朗普挥之不去的问题。

sentences.en: But it feels like the picture that's emerging, at least from your reporting, is that we already kind of know the answer about how Epstein became Epstein in some way,
sentences.zh: 但感觉正在浮现的真相——至少从你们的报道来看——是我们其实已经多少知道了关于爱泼斯坦是如何成为后来的爱泼斯坦的答案，

sentences.en: which is that he didn't need to be a secret spy or whatever these other conspiracy theories that have popped up in intervening years would suggeSt.
sentences.zh: 那就是他不需要成为什么秘密间谍，也不需要像近年来冒出来的其他阴谋论所暗示的那样。

sentences.en: He just needed to be a remarkably savvy guy who learned very early on that he could manipulate people, he could commit crimes,
sentences.zh: 他只需要成为一个极其精明的人，很早就懂得了自己可以操纵他人、可以犯罪，

sentences.en: and he could basically get away with anything he wanted as he climbed up the ladder.
sentences.zh: 并且在步步高升的过程中基本上可以逃脱任何他想做的事。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这是对的。

sentences.en: And I think there's been a lot of really good reporting that has peeled back a lot of layers of the Epstein story.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为有很多非常精彩的报道，剥丝抽茧般揭开了爱泼斯坦故事的很多层内幕。

sentences.en: I do think that there are still a bunch of layers left to unpeel, and I'm not holding out a huge degree of confidence
sentences.zh: 我的确认为仍然有许多层内幕有待揭开，而且我并不抱有太大的信心

sentences.en: that these files, as they get released, are going to do much of that peeling.
sentences.zh: 认为这些文件在公开时会做多少这样的揭秘。

sentences.en: But I do think there are still a ton of important questions that have not been answered.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为仍有大量尚未解答的重要问题。

sentences.en: And I think the Epstein saga for years now has been kind of a political Rorschach test, and that people on the left, or many people on the left,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为多年来爱泼斯坦事件一直像是一种政治罗夏测验，左翼人士，或者许多左翼人士，

sentences.en: view it as a weapon with which to go after Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 将其视为攻击唐纳德·特朗普的武器。

sentences.en: I think on the right, a lot of people view this as a vehicle to attack kind of liberal globalist institutions and individuals.
sentences.zh: 我认为在右翼，许多人将此视为攻击某种自由派全球主义机构和个人的工具。

sentences.en: And I think the truth is probably somewhere in the middle, right?
sentences.zh: 我想真相可能介于两者之间，对吧？

sentences.en: That there are a lot of very rich, powerful men who enabled Epstein and may have participated in some of his crimes.
sentences.zh: 那就是有许多非常富有、权势熏天的男士助长了爱泼斯坦的行为，并可能参与了他的一些犯罪活动。

sentences.en: I do not think that there has been very much accountability for those men yet, and I don't think that we have a full sense of what information may or may not be
sentences.zh: 我认为这些男士目前还没有受到太多的清算，而且我们对于这些政府文件中可能包含或不包含哪些

sentences.en: in these government files pertaining to those men.
sentences.zh: 与这些男士相关的信息，并没有一个全面的了解。

sentences.en: But I think the reason people think that there may be more shoes to drop, it's partly that their dreams of having their political enemies
sentences.zh: 但我认为人们觉得还会有更多靴子落地的原因，一部分是因为他们希望自己的政治对手

sentences.en: crushed by the Epstein scandal remain unfulfilled.
sentences.zh: 被爱泼斯坦丑闻粉碎的梦想尚未实现。

sentences.en: But it's also partly a recognition that there were so many people involved in supporting Epstein and allowing his criminal network to prosper
sentences.zh: 但这也部分源于这样一种认知：有太多的人参与了支持爱泼斯坦并纵容其犯罪网络繁荣发展，

sentences.en: that it just doesn't feel right that only two people,
sentences.zh: 以至于只有两个人——

sentences.en: Jeffrey Epstein and his associate Ghislaine Maxwell, have really been held to account for this so far.
sentences.zh: 杰弗里·爱泼斯坦和他的同伙吉斯莱恩·马克斯韦尔——真正为此承担了责任，这让人觉得很不公正。

sentences.en: Okay, but speaking of being held accountable,
sentences.zh: 好的，但说到承担责任，

sentences.en: I do wonder if that's the takeaway here.
sentences.zh: 我确实想知道这是否就是我们应得的结论。

sentences.en: Because on the one hand, obviously, Jeffrey Epstein died in a jail cell.
sentences.zh: 因为一方面，显而易见，杰弗里·爱泼斯坦死在了狱室里。

sentences.en: On the other hand, he got away with horrific crimes and amassed so much money and power over the years.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，他犯下了可怕的罪行却逍遥法外，多年来聚敛了巨额财富和权力。

sentences.en: Because we've been talking this whole conversation about the lessons that Epstein learned in order to do that.
sentences.zh: 因为我们在整个对话中一直在讨论爱泼斯坦为了做到这一点而吸取的教训。

sentences.en: But I do wonder what lessons we as the public should learn looking at Epstein's story and how he came to an end.
sentences.zh: 但我确实想知道，我们作为公众，在回顾爱泼斯坦的故事及其结局时，应该吸取什么教训。

sentences.en: Well, look, dying in a jail cell is no one's idea of a happy ending.
sentences.zh: 嗯，听着，死在狱室里绝不是任何人眼中的大团圆结局。

sentences.en: That said, the story of Epstein is really one of impunity.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，爱泼斯坦的故事确实是一个关于特权的典型故事。

sentences.en: And he, as you said, got away with this for years, despite repeated red flags, despite many warnings, despite many victims coming forward and trying to blow the whistle on him.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，尽管一再出现危险信号，尽管有许多警告，尽管有许多受害者站出来试图揭发他，他还是逍遥法外多年。

sentences.en: And to me, it's also a broader story of impunity, not just about Jeffrey Epstein, but the people around him, many of whom really have not had a public reckoning
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这也是一个更广泛的特权故事，不仅仅关于杰弗里·爱泼斯坦，还关于他周围的人，他们中的许多人确实没有在公众面前

sentences.en: about the roles they play in this.
sentences.zh: 为他们在其中扮演的角色进行清算。

sentences.en: The reason that people remain obsessed about Epstein, to a large degree, I think, is that there are so many people out there who have not had a similar public reckoning.
sentences.zh: 我认为，人们在很大程度上仍然痴迷于爱泼斯坦的原因，在于有太多这样的人还没有经历类似的公开清算。

sentences.en: And so, to me, that's the great takeaway, that for people with a lot of money and power and connections, they really can act with impunity.
sentences.zh: 所以，对我们来说，这就是最大的启示：对于那些拥有大量财富、权力和人脉的人来说，他们确实可以为所欲为而无需承担后果。

sentences.en: David Enrich, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 大卫·恩里奇，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: Late on Monday night, the Department of Justice released more files related to the investigation of Jeffrey Epstein.
sentences.zh: 周一深夜，司法部公布了更多与调查杰弗里·爱泼斯坦相关的文件。

sentences.en: The documents contained hundreds of references to President Trump, although most of them are from media reports, unverified tips, and discussions among investigators,
sentences.zh: 这些文件包含数百处提及特朗普总统的地方，尽管其中大部分来自媒体报道、未经证实的线索以及调查人员之间的讨论，

sentences.zh: 其中包括一条提及特朗普在1993年至1996年间曾八次乘坐爱泼斯坦的私人飞机。

sentences.en: None of the mentions appear to be evidence of wrongdoing.
